title: Six-class rho on secp256k1, step priced from compiled AArch64 kernels with an assembly subtraction

claims.statement: For uniform full-production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho attack specified in proof.md halts on every run after at most 2^126.60 target-group-operation equivalents: a global meter charges every action before it runs. The ordinary step is not charged as a reference addition plus allowance; it is charged at its counted scalar AArch64 instructions, 860 instructions = 0.860 units of C=1000 (counted 123 + 597 instructions per walk for the two loop passes of kernels/secp_walk.c, clang -O3 -target aarch64-linux-gnu with a nine-instruction inline-assembly modular subtraction, shipped as kernels/secp_loops.s and counted by experiment.py, plus 129 instruction allowances for the class bookkeeping rows, 849 in all). The kernels are 4x64-bit limb code for p=2^256-2^32-977 (multiplication, squaring, subtraction, canonicalisation, libsecp256k1 inversion chain shared by a batch of >=2^15 walks at under one instruction per walk) and are tested against Python big integers and affine arithmetic. Traversal costs 0.890, doubling at most 2.0, and no reference operation is also charged. Under the disclosed H1 random-mapping heuristic, the chance of recovery is greater than 0.3905 after a Markov early-halt bound below 0.0045 and all other loss events. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units and included; no nonuniform advice. The walk, class key, canonical-index rule, cycle handling, phases, storage and heuristic are those of submission a9f1a6fe (six-class-rho-secp-counted-v1, 126.65), itself built on 3682292 (six-class-rho-secp-147-v1), 758d8df6 and 189ebc42; all are credited dependencies but no prior verdict is a mathematical premise. This is an analytical, heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the field kernels checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, instruction counts parsed from the shipped AArch64 assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
